title: Financial Analysis
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `summarize(transactions)`. The input is a list of strings representing financial records, where each string contains a date, a transaction type, and an amount separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the strings into components. Another helper normalizes the amounts to a standard format. A third helper aggregates the normalized amounts by transaction type. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns a list of tuples containing the type and the total amount. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string 10 may deposit 50 and the string 12 may withdrawal 20. Example output: list containing one tuple deposit 50 and one tuple withdrawal 20.

title: Bioinformatics Sequence Analysis
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `evaluate(sequence)`. The input is a single long string of letters representing a biological sequence. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper validates the sequence by ensuring it only contains valid base letters. The second helper transcribes the sequence by replacing certain letters to simulate biological processes. The third helper calculates the percentage of specific target bases in the entire sequence. The entry function uses these helpers and returns a list containing the valid transcribed sequence and the calculated percentage. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: the string acgt. Example output: list containing the string acgu and the number 50.

title: Text Readability Scorer
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `score(text)`. The input is a long string of prose. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper splits the text into sentences based on punctuation. Another helper tokenizes sentences into individual words and removes punctuation. A third helper estimates the number of syllables in a word by counting vowel groups. The entry function coordinates these steps to compute a final numerical reading grade based on average words per sentence and average syllables per word, returning this single number. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: the string hello there how are you today. Example output: the number 4.

title: Geometry Bounding Box
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `enclose(shapes)`. The input is a list of strings where each string describes a shape, such as circle with center coordinates and radius, or rectangle with corner coordinates. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the shape strings into numerical coordinates and shape types. Another helper calculates the extreme minimum and maximum points for a circle. A third helper calculates the extreme points for a rectangle. The entry function uses these helpers to find the global minimum and maximum coordinates that enclose all shapes, returning them as a list of four numbers. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string circle 0 0 5. Example output: list containing the numbers minus 5, minus 5, 5, 5.

title: Inventory Restock
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `restock(items)`. The input is a list of strings representing inventory items, containing the item name, current stock, threshold, and reorder amount separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the strings into item details. The second helper identifies items whose current stock is strictly below the threshold. The third helper calculates the estimated cost of restocking based on a fixed ten dollar unit price for all items. The entry function uses these helpers to return a list of tuples containing the item name and the total restock cost. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string apples 5 10 20. Example output: list containing one tuple apples 200.

title: Log File Alert
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `monitor(logs)`. The input is a list of strings representing server logs, each with a timestamp, severity level, service name, and message separated by commas. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper splits the log strings into their four components. Another helper filters the logs to retain only those with a severity level of critical or error. A third helper groups the filtered logs by service name and counts them. The entry function coordinates these steps and returns a list of tuples containing the service name and its error count. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string morning, error, database, timeout. Example output: list containing one tuple database 1.

title: Music Transposition
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `transpose(data)`. The input is a list containing exactly two elements: a string of musical notes separated by spaces, and an integer shift amount. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper splits the string into individual note names. Another helper converts a note name to its corresponding integer position on a twelve tone scale. A third helper applies the shift amount and wraps it around to return the new note name. The entry function uses these helpers to return a string of the transposed notes separated by spaces. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string c d e and the number 2. Example output: the string d e f sharp.

title: Recipe Scaler
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `scale(recipe)`. The input is a list of strings representing ingredients, each with a numerical amount, a unit of measurement, and an ingredient name, followed by a final string representing the scaling multiplier. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper extracts the multiplier from the end of the list and isolates the ingredient strings. The second helper parses an ingredient string into its amount, unit, and name. The third helper multiplies the amount by the scaling factor and formats the new string. The entry function coordinates these steps and returns a list of scaled ingredient strings. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string 2 cups flour and the string 1.5. Example output: list containing the string 3.0 cups flour.

title: Shift Scheduling
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `schedule(requests)`. The input is a list of strings, each containing a start time and an end time in minutes separated by a space. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the time strings into pairs of integers. Another helper sorts the time pairs based on the start time. A third helper iterates through the sorted pairs and merges any overlapping time blocks into continuous intervals. The entry function coordinates these steps and returns a list of non overlapping interval tuples. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string 0 10 and the string 5 15. Example output: list containing one tuple 0 15.

title: Sensor Data Smoothing
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `smooth(readings)`. The input is a list of strings where each string is a raw numerical sensor reading. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper converts the strings into floating point numbers. Another helper filters out values that are less than zero or greater than one hundred, considering them invalid. A third helper applies a simple moving average by replacing each valid reading with the average of itself and its immediate valid neighbors. The entry function uses these helpers and returns a list of the smoothed numbers. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the strings 10, 20, 150, 30. Example output: list containing the numbers 15.0, 20.0, 25.0.

title: Cryptography Cipher
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `encrypt(message)`. The input is a single string of plain text. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper cleans the text by converting it to lowercase and removing all spaces and punctuation. The second helper applies a fixed character shift of three positions forward in the alphabet to a given letter. The third helper chunks the transformed text into blocks of five characters separated by spaces. The entry function coordinates these helpers to process the message and returns the final encrypted string. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: the string hello world. Example output: the string khoor zruog.

title: Astronomical Orbits
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `classify(bodies)`. The input is a list of strings where each represents an astronomical body, containing its name, semi major axis, and eccentricity separated by commas. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the string into the name, a distance float, and an eccentricity float. Another helper calculates the orbital period based on the distance using simplified kepler laws. A third helper classifies the orbit as circular if eccentricity is near zero, or elliptical otherwise. The entry function coordinates these steps and returns a list of tuples containing the name, period, and classification. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string earth, 1.0, 0.016. Example output: list containing one tuple earth, 1.0, circular.

title: Weather Anomalies
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `analyze(temperatures)`. The input is a list of strings containing a date and a daily high temperature in fahrenheit separated by a colon. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the strings into dates and fahrenheit integers. The second helper converts the fahrenheit values to celsius. The third helper calculates the average celsius temperature across all provided days. The entry function coordinates these steps and returns a list of dates where the celsius temperature was strictly greater than the calculated average. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string monday: 50 and the string tuesday: 70. Example output: list containing the string tuesday.

title: Text Game Combat
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `resolve(actions)`. The input is a list of strings representing combat turns, each containing an attacker name, attack power, and target defense separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the action string into a name and two integer values. Another helper calculates the net damage by subtracting defense from attack, returning zero if the result is negative. A third helper applies a flat combo bonus of five extra damage for any attack that originally had more than twenty power. The entry function coordinates these calculations and returns a list of tuples containing the attacker name and the final damage dealt. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string hero 25 10. Example output: list containing one tuple hero 20.

title: Traffic Simulation
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `simulate(cars)`. The input is a list of strings, each containing a car identifier, its current speed, and the speed limit separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the strings into an identifier and two integers. The second helper calculates an adjusted speed by reducing the current speed by ten if it exceeds the speed limit, or keeping it the same otherwise. The third helper calculates the travel time to cover a distance of one hundred miles using the adjusted speed. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns a list of tuples containing the car identifier and the calculated travel time. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string car 60 50. Example output: list containing one tuple car 2.0.

title: Election Vote Counter
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `tally(ballots)`. The input is a list of strings where each string is a comma separated list of candidates ranked by a single voter. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper extracts the first choice candidate from a ballot string by taking the first name before the comma. Another helper updates a global frequency tally for a given candidate. A third helper identifies the candidate with the absolute highest number of first choice votes from the final tally. The entry function coordinates these steps and returns the name of the winning candidate as a string. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string alice, bob and the string alice, charlie. Example output: the string alice.

title: Graph Connectivity
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `analyze(edges)`. The input is a list of strings where each string contains two node names separated by a space, representing a connection in a network. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the connection strings and populates an adjacency structure. The second helper traverses the network from a given starting node to find all reachable nodes. The third helper iterates over all nodes to find and collect all distinct isolated groups of connected nodes. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns the total number of distinct groups found in the network. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string node1 node2 and the string node3 node4. Example output: the number 2.

title: Chess Board Evaluation
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `evaluate(board)`. The input is a list of strings where each string represents a piece on a board, containing its color, type, and position separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the piece strings into their respective properties. Another helper assigns a standard point value to the piece based on its type, such as nine for a queen and one for a pawn. A third helper tallies the total score for a specific color by summing the values of all pieces. The entry function uses these helpers to calculate the scores for both white and black, and returns the numerical difference between white and black. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string white queen e4 and the string black pawn d5. Example output: the number 8.

title: Network Routing
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `route(packets)`. The input is a list of strings representing network packets, each containing a destination, a payload size in bytes, and a priority level separated by commas. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the packet strings into components. The second helper calculates the expected transmission delay by multiplying the payload size by a fixed latency factor of two. The third helper filters out any packets that have a delay exceeding one hundred and a low priority level. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns a list of destination strings for the packets that successfully pass the filter. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string server, 60, low. Example output: an empty list.

title: Retail Discount Calculator
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `checkout(cart)`. The input is a list of strings representing purchased items, containing the item name, the category, and the price separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the item strings into their components. Another helper applies a discount by reducing the price by twenty percent if the category is electronics. A third helper calculates an eight percent sales tax on the discounted price. The entry function coordinates these steps, sums up the final prices including tax for all items, and returns the total as a single number rounded to two decimal places. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string laptop electronics 1000. Example output: the number 864.0.

title: Survey Normalization
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `normalize(responses)`. The input is a list of strings, each containing a participant name and their raw score out of ten, separated by a colon. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the strings into names and integer scores. The second helper calculates the average score across all participants. The third helper standardizes a score by subtracting the average and dividing by the average, producing a relative performance metric. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns a list of tuples containing the participant name and their relative metric. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string john: 8 and the string jane: 2. Example output: list containing one tuple john 0.6 and one tuple jane minus 0.6.

title: Tournament Bracket
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `simulate(teams)`. The input is a list of strings, each containing a team name and an integer power rating separated by a space. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the team strings into names and ratings. Another helper takes two teams and determines the winner by comparing their power ratings, favoring the strictly higher rating or the first team in a tie. A third helper processes a full round of matches by pairing adjacent teams in the list and collecting the winners. The entry function repeatedly calls the round helper until only one team remains, returning the name of the overall champion. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string lions 50 and the string tigers 60. Example output: the string tigers.

title: File System Mock
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `inspect(files)`. The input is a list of strings representing files, each containing a file path and a size in kilobytes separated by a space. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper parses the string into a path and an integer size. The second helper extracts the top level folder name from the path by taking the portion before the first slash. The third helper accumulates the file sizes into a running total for a specific top level folder. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns a list of tuples containing the folder name and its total size in kilobytes. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string docs/resume 100 and the string docs/photo 500. Example output: list containing one tuple docs 600.

title: Sports Statistics
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `compile(matches)`. The input is a list of strings representing game results, each containing a home team, away team, home goals, and away goals separated by spaces. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. One helper parses the match strings into team names and integer goals. Another helper determines the points earned by the home team, awarding three for a win, one for a draw, and zero for a loss. A third helper similarly determines the points earned by the away team. The entry function uses these helpers to aggregate the total points for every team and returns a list of tuples containing the team name and total points. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the string red blue 2 1. Example output: list containing one tuple red 3 and one tuple blue 0.

title: Image Filter Mock
spec: Write a well-documented module with an entry function `process(pixels)`. The input is a list of integer pixel values ranging from zero to two hundred fifty five. The module must contain at least three additional helper functions. The first helper converts the flat list into a two dimensional grid with a fixed width of three columns. The second helper applies a threshold to a single pixel, returning two hundred fifty five if the value is above one hundred, or zero otherwise. The third helper iterates over the grid and applies the threshold to every pixel. The entry function coordinates these helpers and returns the processed grid flattened back into a single list of integers. Include detailed multi-line descriptions for the module and every function explaining their purpose, arguments, and return values. Example input: list containing the numbers 50, 150, 90. Example output: list containing the numbers 0, 255, 0.

title: Satellite Telemetry Parsing
spec: The main entry point receives a list of lists representing raw satellite signals. Write a dedicated helper function to extract the timestamp and coordinates from a single reading. Write another helper function to validate if the coordinates are within valid earthly bounds. Write a third helper function to convert the signal strength into a standardized percentage out of one hundred. Finally, use these in the main function `process(telemetry)` to process all readings, discarding invalid ones and returning a list of tuples containing the timestamp, converted coordinates, and signal percentage. Example input: [[1620000000, 45, -90, 80], [1620000010, 200, -90, 70]]. Example output: [(1620000000, 45, -90, 80)].

title: E-commerce Tax Calculator
spec: The main routine takes a list of purchase amounts. Create a distinct helper function to determine the base tax rate based on the amount threshold, where amounts over one hundred get a ten percent rate and others get five percent. Create another helper function to apply a special exemption discount if the amount ends in a five. Create a third helper function to compute the final price by combining the base amount, tax, and exemptions. The main routine `tax(purchases)` should return a list of final prices. Example input: [50, 105]. Example output: [52.5, 110.25].

title: Word Game Scoring
spec: The primary function evaluates a list of played words. Implement a helper function to calculate the base score of a word by counting each letter as one point. Implement a second helper function to double the score if the word contains the letter x or z. Implement a third helper function to add a fifty point bonus if the word is seven or more letters long. The primary function `score(words)` processes each word and returns a list of integer scores. Example input: ["cat", "xylophone"]. Example output: [3, 68].

title: Logistics Routing Cost
spec: The entry point accepts a list of trip distances in miles. Write a helper function to calculate the fuel cost assuming three dollars per gallon and fifteen miles per gallon. Write another helper function to estimate tolls, adding five dollars for every fifty miles traveled. Write a third helper function to add a twenty dollar driver fee for any trip over one hundred miles. Return a list of total costs for each trip from the main entry point `estimate(trips)`. Example input: [30, 120]. Example output: [6.0, 59.0].

title: Warehouse Packaging Estimator
spec: The main function processes a list of item weights in pounds. Write a helper function to determine the base box size, returning small for under five pounds and large otherwise. Write a second helper function to calculate the packaging material cost, which is two dollars for small boxes and five dollars for large boxes. Write a third helper function to add a handling fee of one dollar for any item weighing over ten pounds. The main function `package(weights)` should use these to return a list of total packaging costs for each item. Example input: [3, 12]. Example output: [2.0, 6.0].

title: Solar Panel Energy Estimator
spec: The entry function receives a list of daily sunlight hours for various panels. Implement a helper function to calculate the base energy yield by multiplying hours by two hundred watts. Implement another helper function to apply a ten percent efficiency loss if the hours exceed ten due to overheating. Implement a third helper function to convert the final wattage into kilowatt hours by dividing by one thousand. The entry function `yields(panels)` returns a list of total kilowatt hours for each panel. Example input: [5, 12]. Example output: [1.0, 2.16].

title: Coffee Shop Loyalty Program
spec: The main routine takes a list of current customer point totals. Create a helper function to calculate points earned from a new purchase of five dollars, awarding two points per dollar. Create a second helper function to check if the total points exceed one hundred, qualifying for a free drink. Create a third helper function to deduct one hundred points if a free drink is awarded. The main routine `loyalty(customers)` assumes each customer makes a five dollar purchase and returns a list of their updated point totals. Example input: [90, 50]. Example output: [0, 60].

title: Real Estate Valuation
spec: The primary function handles a list of tuples containing square footage and age in years. Write a separate helper function to calculate the base price at one hundred and fifty per square foot. Write another helper function to apply an age penalty, deducting one thousand for every year over ten. Write a third helper function to add a twenty percent premium if the square footage is over two thousand. The primary function `appraise(properties)` returns a list of final appraised values. Example input: [(1500, 5), (2500, 15)]. Example output: [225000, 444000].

title: Healthcare Risk Assessment
spec: The entry point evaluates a list of tuples containing weight in kilograms and height in meters. Implement a helper function to calculate the body mass index by dividing weight by height squared. Implement a second helper function to categorize the index into normal, overweight, or obese based on standard medical thresholds. Implement a third helper function to flag high risk if the category is obese. The entry point `assess(patients)` should return a list of risk categories for each patient. Example input: [(70, 1.75), (100, 1.6)]. Example output: ["normal", "obese"].

title: Academic Grading System
spec: The main function processes a list of raw student exam scores. Create a helper function to apply a curve that adds five points to each score, capped at one hundred. Create another helper function to convert a numerical score into a letter grade, where ninety and above is an a, and eighty and above is a b. Create a third helper function to determine if the student passed, which requires a c or higher. Return a list of tuples containing the curved score and letter grade for each student from `grade(scores)`. Example input: [85, 96]. Example output: [(90, "a"), (100, "a")].

title: Public Transit Fare Calculator
spec: The entry function accepts a list of integers representing the number of zones traveled. Write a helper function to calculate the base fare of two plus one per zone. Write a second helper function to apply a peak hour surcharge of fifty percent if the trip occurs during rush hour, which for this exercise we assume applies to all trips over three zones. Write a third helper function to apply a senior discount of one dollar on the final fare. Return a list of calculated fares using `fare(trips)`. Example input: [2, 5]. Example output: [4.0, 9.5].

title: Water Quality Monitoring
spec: The primary routine takes a list of tuples containing acidity level and turbidity. Implement a helper function to check if the acidity is strictly between six point five and eight point five. Implement another helper function to verify that turbidity is below five. Implement a third helper function to determine the overall safety status, marking the sample as safe only if both checks pass. The main routine `quality(samples)` processes all samples and returns a list of boolean values indicating safety. Example input: [(7.0, 3.0), (5.0, 2.0)]. Example output: [true, false].

title: Cinema Ticket Pricing
spec: The main entry point receives a list of customer ages. Create a helper function to set the base ticket price at fifteen. Create a second helper function to apply a child discount of five if the age is under twelve, and a senior discount of three if the age is over sixty five. Create a third helper function to add a booking fee of one to every ticket. The main entry point `tickets(requests)` should return a list of final ticket prices. Example input: [10, 40, 70]. Example output: [11, 16, 13].

title: Drone Flight Path Validator
spec: The entry function processes a list of tuples containing flight altitude and battery percentage. Write a separate helper function to check if the altitude is strictly between one hundred and four hundred feet. Write another helper function to verify the battery is above thirty percent. Write a third helper function to approve the flight only if both altitude and battery conditions are met. Return a list of strings stating either approved or denied for each flight using `validate(flights)`. Example input: [(200, 50), (500, 80)]. Example output: ["approved", "denied"].

title: Fitness Tracker Daily Summary
spec: The main function evaluates a list of daily step counts. Implement a helper function to convert steps into estimated calories burned by dividing the count by twenty. Implement a second helper function to convert steps into active minutes by dividing the count by one hundred. Implement a third helper function to determine if a daily goal of ten thousand steps was reached. The main function `summarize(days)` returns a list of tuples containing calories, active minutes, and goal status. Example input: [5000, 12000]. Example output: [(250, 50, false), (600, 120, true)].

title: Restaurant Tip Distributor
spec: The primary function takes a list of total tips collected during various shifts. Create a helper function to calculate the kitchen share, which is twenty percent of the total tips. Create another helper function to calculate the waitstaff share, which receives the remaining eighty percent. Create a third helper function to divide the waitstaff share equally among four servers. The primary function `distribute(shifts)` returns a list of tuples with the kitchen share and the individual server share for each shift. Example input: [100, 200]. Example output: [(20, 20), (40, 40)].

title: Library Fine Calculator
spec: The main entry point receives a list of integers representing days a book is overdue. Write a helper function to calculate the standard fine at twenty five cents per day. Write a second helper function to apply a maximum cap of ten dollars so no fine exceeds this amount. Write a third helper function to waive the fine entirely if it is less than one dollar as a grace policy. Return a list of final fine amounts from the main entry point `fines(returns)`. Example input: [2, 10, 50]. Example output: [0.0, 2.5, 10.0].

title: Hotel Booking Cost
spec: The entry function processes a list of nights stayed. Implement a separate helper function to calculate the room cost at one hundred per night. Implement another helper function to add a flat cleaning fee of fifty to every stay regardless of length. Implement a third helper function to apply a ten percent discount to the room cost if the stay is seven nights or longer. The main function `booking(stays)` returns a list of total costs for each stay. Example input: [2, 10]. Example output: [250.0, 950.0].

title: Electric Vehicle Charging Planner
spec: The primary routine accepts a list of distances in miles to various destinations. Create a helper function to determine how many full charges are needed, assuming a range of two hundred miles per charge. Create a second helper function to calculate the charging time, assuming each full charge takes forty five minutes. Create a third helper function to calculate the total driving time at sixty miles per hour. The primary routine `plan(routes)` returns a list of total trip times in minutes. Example input: [100, 500]. Example output: [100, 590].

title: Online Course Completion Tracker
spec: The main function evaluates a list of tuples containing video completion percentage and final quiz score. Write a helper function to verify the video completion is at least ninety percent. Write another helper function to check if the quiz score is passing, requiring a minimum of seventy. Write a third helper function to grant a certificate if both completion and quiz criteria are satisfied. The main function `progress(students)` should return a list of boolean values indicating certificate eligibility. Example input: [(95, 80), (80, 90)]. Example output: [true, false].

title: Gardening Harvest Predictor
spec: The entry point takes a list of integers representing weeks of growth for various tomato plants. Implement a helper function to calculate base yield, giving two tomatoes per week of growth. Implement a second helper function to subtract three tomatoes if the growth period is under five weeks due to immaturity. Implement a third helper function to cap the maximum yield at twenty tomatoes per plant. Return a list of predicted yields for each plant from `predict(plants)`. Example input: [4, 12]. Example output: [5, 20].

title: Freelance Invoice Generator
spec: The primary function receives a list of hours worked on different projects. Create a helper function to calculate the gross pay at fifty per hour. Create another helper function to apply a five percent discount if the project required more than forty hours. Create a third helper function to add a flat fifteen fee to cover software licensing on every project. The primary function `invoice(projects)` processes each project and returns a list of final invoice totals. Example input: [10, 50]. Example output: [515.0, 2390.0].

title: Smart Home Temperature Controller
spec: The main routine processes a list of current room temperatures in degrees. Write a separate helper function to calculate the difference from a target temperature of seventy two degrees. Write a second helper function to decide the mode, returning heat if the difference is negative and cool if positive. Write a third helper function to determine the fan speed, setting it to high if the absolute difference is more than five degrees and low otherwise. Return a list of tuples containing mode and fan speed using `thermostat(readings)`. Example input: [65, 75]. Example output: [("heat", "high"), ("cool", "low")].

title: Pet Shelter Dietary Planner
spec: The entry function accepts a list of animal weights in pounds. Implement a helper function to calculate the base daily food requirement as one cup per ten pounds of weight. Implement another helper function to add an extra half cup if the animal weighs less than twenty pounds to support growth. Implement a third helper function to round the final amount to the nearest whole cup. The entry function `diet(animals)` returns a list of total daily cups for each animal. Example input: [15, 50]. Example output: [2, 5].

title: Cloud Storage Biller
spec: The main function evaluates a list of storage usage in gigabytes. Create a helper function to calculate the base cost at two cents per gigabyte. Create a second helper function to waive the base cost entirely if the usage is under five gigabytes as part of a free tier. Create a third helper function to add a mandatory network fee of one dollar to all accounts, even those in the free tier. Return a list of final monthly bills in dollars from the main function `bill(accounts)`. Example input: [4, 100]. Example output: [1.0, 3.0].

title: Matrix Math Toolkit
spec: Implement a main function `analyze(matrix)` that takes a square two dimensional list of integers. The process must systematically break down the input by evaluating its transpose, calculating its main diagonal sum, and computing its anti diagonal sum. Require distinct helper components to isolate the row to column inversion, the top left to bottom right extraction, and the top right to bottom left extraction. Return a tuple containing the transposed two dimensional list, the primary trace integer, and the secondary trace integer. For example given a list of lists containing one two three, four five six, seven eight nine, the result is the transposed list, fifteen, and fifteen.

title: Card Hand Evaluator
spec: Create a function `evaluate(hand)` that accepts a list of five tuples where each tuple holds an integer rank and a suit character. The evaluation must be divided into independent helper operations for checking a flush, checking a straight, identifying four of a kind, and finding a full house to determine the highest hand value. Return an integer from one to five representing the hand strength where five is a straight flush and one is a high card. Separating the rank counting, suit grouping, and sequential checking into their own logical routines is necessary for accurate scoring. For example given five tuples with consecutive ranks and the same suit, the result is five.

title: Web Address Deconstructor
spec: Write a function `parse(url)` that takes a plain string representing a web address and extracts its components. The logic must rely on isolated helper routines to independently extract the protocol scheme, the domain host, the port number if present, and the resource path. Process these segments by splitting on the colon slash slash sequence, separating the domain from the port using a colon, and locating the first slash for the path. Return a tuple of four elements containing the scheme, host, integer port, and path defaulting to standard values if missing. For example inputting http colon slash slash localhost colon eight thousand slash index yields a tuple of http, localhost, eight thousand, and slash index.

title: Ten Pin Scorer
spec: Provide a function `score(rolls)` that accepts a list of integers representing the pins knocked down in each roll of a game. The scoring logic must cleanly differentiate using distinct helper operations for calculating the bonus for a strike, calculating the bonus for a spare, and summing an open frame. The sequence must advance frame by frame up to the tenth frame by checking if the first roll is ten or if two consecutive rolls sum to ten. Return the total integer score of the game. An input of twelve tens representing a perfect game results in three hundred.

title: Global Time Shift
spec: Design a function `convert(timestamp)` that receives a tuple containing an integer hour, integer minute, and an integer offset representing a coordinated universal time adjustment. The logic must cleanly separate into individual routines the extraction of the base time, the calculation of the adjusted hour, and the day wrap around mathematics. Adjust the hour by adding the offset, wrapping past twenty four or below zero while incrementing or decrementing a day counter. Return a tuple with the new day offset, new hour, and original minute. Given zero, thirty, and minus five, the result is minus one, nineteen, and thirty.

title: Color Format Converter
spec: Implement `transform(color)` taking a tuple of three integers representing red, green, and blue values from zero to two hundred fifty five. The conversion must utilize separate routines to individually calculate the hue, calculate the saturation, and calculate the lightness by first finding the maximum and minimum color components. Separate the logic for determining the delta difference, the assignment of the hue based on which color component is maximum, and the percentage scaling for saturation. Return a tuple of three integers representing hue in degrees, saturation percentage, and lightness percentage. For example pure red at two hundred fifty five, zero, zero yields zero, one hundred, and fifty.

title: Password Complexity Validator
spec: Create a function `validate(password)` that processes a plain string to determine its security level. The validation must use separate helper routines to independently assess if the string exceeds eight characters, contains at least one uppercase letter, includes at least one digit, and possesses a special punctuation mark. Tally these independent boolean criteria into a total score from zero to four. Return this integer score indicating the strength of the password. An input string of Password followed by the number one and an exclamation mark results in a score of four.

title: Rational Number Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(fractions)` that accepts a list of tuples where each tuple is a numerator and denominator integer pair. The logic must rely on distinct mathematical routines to find the greatest common divisor, compute the least common multiple for denominators, and simplify the resulting fraction. Processing the cross multiplication and the final reduction must be handled as isolated arithmetic operations to avoid overflow while iteratively adding each fraction to a running total. Return a single tuple representing the fully simplified final fraction. Adding one half and one third results in five sixths.

title: Coordinate Distance Calculator
spec: Design a function `measure(points)` that takes two tuples of three integers representing points in three dimensional space. The procedure must compute three different distance metrics by utilizing separate routines for calculating the Euclidean distance, the Manhattan distance, and the Chebyshev maximum absolute difference. Each metric requires its own isolated mathematical aggregation across the horizontal, vertical, and depth axes. Return a tuple of three floating point numbers corresponding to each metric rounded to two decimal places. For points zero zero zero and one two two, the result is three point zero, five point zero, and two point zero.

title: Gregorian Calendar Math
spec: Implement a function `difference(dates)` that receives two tuples each containing a year, month, and day integer. The logic must determine the total number of days between the two dates by using isolated routines for leap year verification, computing days accumulated in full years, and computing days passed within the current year based on month lengths. Accumulate the absolute day count from a fixed historical epoch for both dates and subtract them. Return the absolute integer difference in days. Given dates of two thousand twenty, one, one and two thousand twenty, one, thirty one, the result is thirty.

title: Algebraic Polynomial Evaluator
spec: Provide a function `resolve(polynomial)` that takes a list of integers representing coefficients from lowest to highest degree and an integer value for the variable x. The logic must include isolated routines for calculating the first derivative of the polynomial, finding the second derivative, and computing the numerical value of the original polynomial at the given x. Apply the power rule incrementally by multiplying each coefficient by its index and shifting the list down. Return a tuple containing the evaluated integer result, the first derivative list, and the second derivative list. An input of one, two, three and an x of two yields seventeen, two and six, and six.

title: Grid Puzzle Validator
spec: Write a function `verify(grid)` that processes a nine by nine list of lists of integers representing a completed puzzle board. The verification must be broken down into separate routines to check all nine horizontal rows for unique digits, check all nine vertical columns, and check all nine three by three subgrids. Each evaluation should independently confirm that the digits one through nine appear exactly once without duplicates. Return a boolean value of true if the entire board is valid or false if any segment fails. A fully correct standard board returns true.

title: Network Boundary Calculator
spec: Create a function `subnet(network)` that takes a tuple containing four integer octets and a prefix integer representing a classless inter domain routing mask. The logic must utilize independent routines to calculate the network address, the broadcast address, and the total usable hosts. Determine the binary mask from the prefix, apply logical bitwise combinations for the network start, and apply inverse combinations for the broadcast end. Return a tuple containing the network tuple, the broadcast tuple, and the usable host integer count. An input of one ninety two, one sixty eight, one, ten with a prefix of twenty four yields the one network, the two fifty five broadcast, and two hundred fifty four hosts.

title: Board Game Arbiter
spec: Design `judge(board)` which accepts a three by three list of lists containing strings of either X, O, or a space character. The arbiter must utilize distinct helper routines to verify horizontal wins, detect vertical wins, scan the two diagonals, and determine if the board is completely full resulting in a draw. Evaluate the lines by checking if all three elements are identical and not empty. Return the winning character if a win is found, the word draw if full, or the word ongoing if spaces remain. A board with three X characters across the top returns X.

title: Record Pagination Engine
spec: Implement `paginate(request)` taking a tuple of an integer total item count, integer items per page, and an integer current page index. The calculation must rely on separate routines for finding the total number of required pages, determining the zero based starting index for the current page, and calculating the ending index. Clamp the current page to ensure it does not exceed the total pages or fall below one. Return a tuple containing total pages, start index, and end index. Given one hundred items, ten per page, and page three, the result is ten, twenty, and thirty.

title: Telegraph Signal Processor
spec: Create `translate(signals)` that accepts a plain string of dots, dashes, and spaces representing telegraph signals. The processor must isolate into separate routines the tasks of splitting the input by triple spaces for words, splitting by single spaces for letters, and looking up the alphanumeric equivalents. Maintain a predefined mapping of standard patterns to alphabet characters and construct the final decoded message by joining the resolved letters. Return the fully translated uppercase plain string. An input of dot dot dot space dash dash dash space dot dot dot yields the string SOS.

title: Antique Numeral Parser
spec: Write a function `decode(numeral)` that takes a plain string representing a classical ancient number. The parser must separate into distinct routines the logic for identifying the value of the current symbol and comparing it to the next symbol to determine if subtraction is needed. Accumulate the total integer value by adding standard symbols and subtracting when a smaller symbol precedes a larger one. Return the final integer total. An input of the letters X I V results in fourteen.

title: Market Arbitrage Finder
spec: Design `detect(rates)` that accepts a list of tuples containing three plain strings representing a source currency, a target currency, and a floating point exchange rate. The logic must isolate into separate operations the extraction of unique currencies, the construction of a directed graph of rates, and the detection of a cycle that yields a product greater than one. Traverse the rates to find if converting a base amount through a sequence of three different currencies results in a profit. Return a boolean value of true if a profitable loop exists. Given favorable cyclic rates for dollars, euros, and pounds, the result is true.

title: Loom Weave Generator
spec: Implement a function `generate(dimensions)` that takes a tuple of two integers for width and height. The generation must systematically separate into distinct routines the creation of the vertical warp threads, the horizontal weft threads, and the checkerboard intersection pattern. Loop through the row and column coordinates, applying an alternating mathematical check to determine if the thread should be over or under. Return a list of lists of strings containing either an O for over or a U for under. A two by two dimension yields a grid with O U on the first row and U O on the second.

title: Snack Dispenser Controller
spec: Write `transact(actions)` that takes a list of tuples where each tuple is an action string and an integer value representing coins inserted or item costs. The controller must maintain a running balance by utilizing isolated routines for adding funds, attempting a purchase by checking if the balance meets the cost, and calculating the remaining change to dispense. Reject purchases if funds are insufficient while keeping the balance intact. Return a tuple of an integer representing successful purchases and an integer representing final returned change. Inserting fifty and buying an item for thirty yields one and twenty.

title: Card Twenty One Scorer
spec: Create `tally(cards)` that receives a list of plain strings representing card faces like Two, Ten, Jack, or Ace. The scoring must separate into distinct routines the aggregation of standard numeric values, the counting of face cards as ten, and the dynamic evaluation of aces as either one or eleven. Sum the initial base values assuming aces are eleven, then iteratively reduce aces to one if the total exceeds twenty one to prevent busting. Return the highest valid integer score. An input of Ace and Nine results in twenty.

title: Distribution Statistician
spec: Design `summarize(samples)` that accepts a list of floating point numbers representing a data population. The evaluation must use independent mathematical routines to calculate the arithmetic mean, compute the variance by finding the squared differences from the mean, and determine the standard deviation. After establishing the core metrics, calculate the standard error based on the sample size. Return a tuple of four floating point numbers representing mean, variance, deviation, and standard error. For a simple list of numbers, the result is their respective statistical boundaries.

title: Simple Text Formatter
spec: Implement `format(document)` taking a list of plain strings representing lines of text. The formatter must employ distinct helper operations to convert lines starting with a hash into heading tags, wrap plain text in paragraph tags, and transform text surrounded by double asterisks into bold tags. Process each line sequentially and apply the specific text replacement before adding it to the final output list. Return a plain string combining all processed lines separated by newlines. An input of a hash and title yields a string wrapped in h one tags.

title: Building Lift Controller
spec: Write a function `simulate(requests)` that takes a list of integers representing destination floors in a building. The logic must isolate into separate routines the determination of the current direction of travel, sorting the pending stops based on the upward or downward trajectory, and calculating the total floors traversed. Advance the lift to the nearest requested floor in the current direction before reversing direction to service remaining requests. Return a tuple of the final floor integer and the total floors moved. A sequence of floors five, two, and eight starting from zero yields floor two and fifteen total floors moved.

title: Contact Number Normalizer
spec: Create `normalize(contacts)` that accepts a list of plain strings representing unformatted phone inputs. The normalization must separate into individual routines the removal of all non numeric characters, the validation that the remaining digits equal exactly ten, and the formatting into a standard layout with parentheses and dashes. Filter the input array and map the valid numeric strings into the structured visual format, dropping any that fail the length check. Return a list of correctly formatted strings. An input of five five five one two three four five six seven with spaces yields a bracketed area code and dashed local number.

title: Podcast Feed Builder
spec: The entry function `generate(episodes)` takes a list of lists where each inner list has the episode title, duration in seconds, and publish date. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct step: parsing the date strings to ensure they are valid, converting the duration from total seconds into an hours minutes seconds format, creating the xml layout for a single episode, and wrapping all episodes into a channel wrapper. The main function will orchestrate these helpers. The xml layout uses simple tags for title, duration, and date. Output the final string. Example: given a list with an episode titled pilot, duration three thousand six hundred, and date two thousand twenty three dash one dash one, it outputs the formatted channel string.

title: Brewery Fermentation Monitor
spec: The entry function `evaluate(readings)` processes a list of daily temperature and gravity readings to determine the health of a fermentation batch. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct phase: filtering out anomalous temperature spikes that last only a single day, calculating the daily rate of gravity change to monitor yeast activity, and checking if the gravity has remained stable for three consecutive days to signal completion. The main function orchestrates these to compile the final status report. Return a sentence summarizing the batch status. For example, if gravity drops by two units daily and then stabilizes, return a success message.

title: Ski Resort Avalanche Risk Assessor
spec: The entry function `assess(conditions)` evaluates snow conditions based on a sequence of daily snowfall amounts and average temperatures. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct calculation: determining the accumulated snow pack over a rolling three day window, calculating the temperature fluctuation index which measures consecutive days of freezing and thawing, and combining these metrics to assign a daily danger level from one to five. The main function orchestrates these to identify any multi day periods where the danger level exceeds three. Return a list of the high risk periods. An input of ten zero snowfall days returns an empty list.

title: Escape Room Puzzle State Manager
spec: The entry function `solve(actions)` processes a sequence of player actions to determine if they successfully escape the room. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for evaluating each independent puzzle: verifying if the sequence of four colored button presses matches the secret code, updating the water level in a tank based on valve turns, checking if a heavy object is placed on a pressure plate, and evaluating the final combination lock. The main function orchestrates these steps in order. Return true if all puzzles are solved, otherwise false. For example, pressing red, blue, green, yellow and turning the main valve might yield a true result.

title: Aquarium Filtration Calculator
spec: The entry function `calculate(parameters)` determines the required water pump size and filter media volume for a given fish tank. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct metric: computing the total water volume based on length, width, and height, adjusting the effective volume by subtracting the space taken by gravel and decorations, determining the minimum required flow rate based on whether the tank houses freshwater or saltwater species, and estimating the liters of bio media needed. The main function will orchestrate these helpers and return a tuple containing the flow rate and media volume. An empty tank of standard dimensions will return the base required flow and zero media.

title: Perfume Fragrance Blender
spec: The entry function `formulate(ingredients)` calculates the final aromatic profile of a custom perfume. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct step: categorizing each essential oil into top, heart, or base notes based on its evaporation rate, normalizing the quantities so the total mixture adds up to one hundred percent, checking if the ratio between the three categories falls within acceptable traditional ranges, and producing a descriptive profile string of the dominant scents. The main function orchestrates these helpers and returns the profile string. For example, an equal mix of lemon, rose, and vanilla might return a balanced floral citrus profile.

title: Apiary Honey Yield Estimator
spec: The entry function `estimate(hives)` predicts the total seasonal honey production for a collection of bee colonies. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct calculation: assessing the strength of each colony based on the number of frames covered by bees, calculating the available foraging area given the local floral density, and adjusting the base yield by applying weather penalty factors for days with excessive rain. The main function orchestrates these to sum the projected kilograms of honey across all hives. Return the total estimated yield as an integer. For example, three strong hives in dense floral areas with good weather might yield one hundred fifty kilograms.

title: Pottery Kiln Firing Profiler
spec: The entry function `profile(segments)` evaluates a proposed heating schedule for a ceramics kiln. The schedule is a list of target temperatures and time durations. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct safety check: verifying that the initial heating ramp is slow enough to prevent moisture explosions in the clay, ensuring the peak temperature is held for the correct amount of time to properly mature the glaze, confirming that the cooling phase drops slowly to avoid thermal shock, and calculating the total energy consumed during the cycle. The main function orchestrates these and returns a string stating if the schedule is safe or rejected. A slow ramp to one thousand degrees over ten hours returns safe.

title: Bicycle Gear Ratio Analyzer
spec: The entry function `analyze(drivetrain)` evaluates the climbing efficiency and top speed potential of a bicycle based on its chainrings and cassette cogs. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct computation: calculating the gear inches for every combination of front chainring and rear cog, identifying the lowest possible gear for steep ascents, finding the highest gear for flat sprints, and determining if there are redundant overlapping gears that provide identical ratios. The main function orchestrates these and returns a list containing the lowest gear, highest gear, and number of unique ratios. A standard setup with fifty teeth in front and twenty in back yields predictable ratios.

title: Scuba Dive Decompression Planner
spec: The entry function `plan(profiles)` calculates the required safety stops for a series of underwater dives. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct phase: tracking the maximum depth and total bottom time for each dive in the sequence, computing the amount of nitrogen absorbed into the tissues, determining the length of surface intervals between dives to allow for off gassing, and prescribing the depth and duration of necessary safety stops before surfacing. The main function orchestrates these steps and returns a list of stop times in minutes. A shallow dive of thirty minutes will return a standard three minute stop.

title: Greenhouse Humidity Controller
spec: The entry function `regulate(sensors)` decides whether to activate misting systems or exhaust fans in a botanical greenhouse. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct evaluation: calculating the current vapor pressure deficit based on temperature and relative humidity readings, comparing this deficit against the optimal range for the specific plant species currently growing, checking the outside weather conditions to see if venting is viable, and deciding on the optimal duration for the fans or misters to run. The main function orchestrates these and returns a string with the chosen action and duration. High humidity inside and low outside will return a fan activation command.

title: Woodworking Cut Optimizer
spec: The entry function `optimize(pieces)` determines the most efficient way to cut smaller required panels out of standard sized plywood sheets. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct algorithmic step: sorting the required pieces from largest to smallest to prioritize difficult fits, checking if a piece can fit horizontally or vertically into the remaining free space of a sheet, tracking the total wasted scrap wood area, and calculating the total number of whole sheets required. The main function orchestrates these and returns the number of sheets and the wasted area. Requesting three small squares from a large board requires one sheet and leaves large scrap.

title: Telescope Lens Focal Calibrator
spec: The entry function `calibrate(measurements)` processes astronomical observations to align a telescope mirror array. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct mathematical operation: calculating the centroid of a star image to determine its exact center, measuring the blur radius to quantify the current focus error, computing the required actuator movements to adjust the primary mirror tilt, and verifying that the proposed adjustments do not exceed the mechanical limits of the motors. The main function orchestrates these and returns the list of actuator adjustments. A perfectly centered star with zero blur returns zero adjustments.

title: Bread Sourdough Starter Tracker
spec: The entry function `track(feedings)` analyzes a log of flour and water additions to assess the vitality of a sourdough culture. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct check: verifying that the hydration level remains constantly at one hundred percent, analyzing the time it takes for the culture to double in volume after each feeding, identifying trends where the doubling time is getting faster or slower, and determining if the culture is ready to be used for baking bread. The main function orchestrates these and returns a sentence indicating readiness. Consistent doubling within four hours returns a ready status.

title: Origami Fold Sequence Validator
spec: The entry function `validate(folds)` checks if a list of paper folding instructions is geometrically possible. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each independent geometric check: ensuring that mountain folds and valley folds alternate correctly in pleated sections, calculating the remaining thickness of the paper to ensure it does not exceed practical physical limits, verifying that corners meet exactly at the intended coordinates, and updating the bounding box of the folded model. The main function orchestrates these and returns a boolean indicating if the sequence is valid. A simple sequence of two valid folds returns true.

title: Museum Exhibit Lighting Director
spec: The entry function `direct(exhibits)` configures the brightness and color temperature of spotlights in an art gallery. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct evaluation: matching the color temperature to the medium of the artwork to enhance colors, limiting the total lux exposure on sensitive historical artifacts to prevent fading, adjusting the beam angle based on the physical size of the painting, and calculating the overall power consumption of the gallery room. The main function orchestrates these and returns a list of brightness percentages for the lights. An oil painting receives warmer, brighter light than a delicate watercolor.

title: Archery Target Score Analyzer
spec: The entry function `score(arrows)` calculates a competitors total match score from a list of arrow coordinates on a target face. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct calculation: computing the radial distance of each arrow from the absolute center, mapping that distance to a point value from one to ten based on the standard ring diameters, detecting if an arrow touches a line to award the higher point value, and counting the perfectly centered arrows used for tiebreakers. The main function orchestrates these to sum the values. Return the total score and the tiebreaker count. An arrow directly in the center returns ten points and one tiebreaker.

title: Train Cargo Weight Balancer
spec: The entry function `balance(cars)` distributes shipping containers across a freight train to ensure safe travel. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each independent step: sorting the containers by weight and hazardous material class, assigning heavy containers toward the front of the train for better braking dynamics, ensuring that adjacent cars do not exceed maximum axle load limits, and verifying that no incompatible hazardous materials are placed next to each other. The main function orchestrates these and returns a list of the container weights in their assigned order.

title: Soap Making Lye Calculator
spec: The entry function `blend(oils)` determines the exact amount of lye and water needed to saponify a blend of fats. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each specific chemical step: calculating the base lye requirement by multiplying the oil weights by their corresponding saponification values, applying a safety discount margin to leave some fats unreacted for skin conditioning, and calculating the required water volume based on a standard concentration ratio. The main function orchestrates these and returns a tuple of lye weight and water weight.

title: Gemstone Carat Appraiser
spec: The entry function `appraise(gems)` estimates the market value of a collection of diamonds and rubies. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct grading step: calculating the base value according to the carat weight and gem type, applying a percentage penalty for visible inclusions or flaws, adding a premium multiplier for exceptional color clarity, and providing a final bundled price if multiple gems of complementary sizes are sold together. The main function orchestrates these and returns the final estimated integer value. A flawless large diamond will yield a very high estimated value.

title: Wind Turbine Output Forecaster
spec: The entry function `forecast(weather)` predicts the electrical power generated by a wind farm over a twenty four hour period. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct calculation: converting the forecasted wind speed at ground level to the effective speed at the turbine hub height, deriving the raw wattage output for that speed using a standard power curve, applying a derating factor if the wind direction is highly turbulent, and cutting off all power generation if speeds exceed the maximum safe operating limit. The main function orchestrates these and returns the total daily megawatt hours.

title: Coffee Roasting Curve Monitor
spec: The entry function `monitor(temperatures)` analyzes a time series of bean temperatures during roasting to ensure flavor quality. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each analytical stage: identifying the turnaround point where the temperature stops dropping and begins to rise, calculating the rate of rise over rolling one minute intervals, detecting the exact minute the first crack occurs based on temperature momentum, and determining the optimal drop time to achieve a medium roast level. The main function orchestrates these and returns the recommended drop time in minutes.

title: Knitting Pattern Expander
spec: The entry function `expand(instructions)` takes a shorthand knitting sequence and generates the stitch by stitch instructions for a single row. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each text processing step: parsing multiplier numbers that dictate how many times to repeat a stitch, expanding bracketed groups of stitches that are repeated as a block, tracking the total stitch count to ensure it matches the required width of the garment, and translating abbreviations into full descriptive words. The main function orchestrates these and returns a list of fully spelled out stitches. A sequence of knit two purl two translates to knit, knit, purl, purl.

title: Soil Nutrient Replenishment Planner
spec: The entry function `replenish(samples)` calculates the exact amount of fertilizer needed for a farm field based on soil tests. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each independent calculation: comparing the current nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels against the optimal baseline for the upcoming crop, determining the required kilograms of each pure nutrient, selecting the most cost effective commercial fertilizer blend that meets these needs without over applying, and calculating the application rate per hectare. The main function orchestrates these and returns a string with the blend name and rate.

title: Synthesizer Oscillator Modulator
spec: The entry function `modulate(waves)` processes a series of digital audio waveforms to apply a frequency modulation effect. Structure the solution into separate helper functions for each distinct mathematical transformation: generating a low frequency oscillator signal to act as the modulator, applying the modulation depth to scale the intensity of the frequency shifts, recalculating the phase of the carrier wave at each sample point, and applying an envelope generator to smoothly fade the sound in and out. The main function orchestrates these and returns a list of the modified audio samples.

title: Meteor Shower Predictor
spec: Implement a small module to predict meteor shower visibility. Include separate functions to calculate the moon illumination penalty, adjust the zenith hourly rate for local light pollution, and determine the viewing quality category. Tie these together in the main entry function `predict(observations)`. The input is a list of tuples where each contains the base peak rate, moon fullness percentage, and a light pollution scale from one to ten. Calculate the effective rate by reducing the base rate by half the moon percentage, then subtracting five for each light pollution point. The quality category is excellent if the effective rate is over fifty, good if over twenty, and poor otherwise. Return a list of tuples with the effective rate and the category. For example, an input of one hundred base rate, fifty percent moon, and light pollution of three returns sixty and excellent.

title: Vinyl Record Appraiser
spec: Write a small module to appraise vintage vinyl records. Provide separate functions to assess the condition multiplier, determine the rarity bonus, and compute the final estimated value. Link these steps in the entry function `appraise(records)`. The input is a list of tuples containing the base price, a condition grade string like mint or good, and the number of known copies. The condition multiplier is two for mint, one for good, and half for poor. The rarity bonus is fifty if known copies are under one hundred, otherwise zero. The final value is the base price times the condition multiplier, plus the rarity bonus. Return a list of final values. For example, a record with base price twenty, mint condition, and fifty copies returns ninety.

title: Ice Cream Mix Stabilizer
spec: Create a small module to analyze homemade ice cream bases. Break the logic into separate functions to sum the total fat content, calculate the required stabilizer weight, and classify the base richness. Coordinate these in the entry function `analyze(ingredients)`. The input is a list of tuples containing ingredient category string and weight in grams. Sum all weights for the fat category and the total base weight. The required stabilizer is zero point five percent of the total base weight. Classify as premium if fat is over fourteen percent of the total weight, standard if over ten, and light otherwise. Return a tuple of stabilizer weight and classification. For example, one hundred grams of fat in a one thousand gram total base returns five grams and standard.

title: Marathon Pace Calculator
spec: Develop a small module to calculate marathon split times and paces. Implement separate functions to convert target finish time to total seconds, calculate the required seconds per mile, and generate a list of mile split times. Drive this logic via the entry function `calculate(target)`. The input is a string representing target time in hours and minutes. Determine the total seconds, then divide by twenty six point two to find the pace in seconds per mile. Generate a list of cumulative times for each of the twenty six miles. Return a tuple containing the pace in seconds and the list of splits. For example, a target of three hours and thirty minutes returns a pace of four hundred and eighty seconds and a list of cumulative times.

title: Book Spine Width Estimator
spec: Write a small module to estimate the spine width of printed books. Provide separate functions to calculate the text block thickness based on page count and paper type, add the cover thickness, and apply a binding tolerance. Use the entry function `estimate(books)` to process the inputs. The input is a list of tuples containing page count, paper weight in grams, and cover type. The text block thickness is the page count divided by two, multiplied by the paper weight divided by one thousand. Add two millimeters for a hardback cover or one millimeter for paperback, plus a ten percent binding tolerance to the total. Return a list of final spine widths in millimeters. For example, three hundred pages, eighty gram paper, and paperback returns thirteen point two millimeters.

title: Tide Pool Safe Time Calculator
