title: Neon Sign Gas Mixture Calculator
spec: Use the entry function `calculate(signs)`. Calculate the gas volumes by processing each sign through specific chemical rules. First, extract the color and length from the text. Second, determine the base gas type: red uses pure neon, blue uses argon, and green uses krypton. Third, compute the volume required: the length multiplied by twelve. Fourth, apply the electrode penalty: add fifteen extra units for neon, ten for argon, and twenty for krypton. Accumulate the totals for each gas type across all signs. Return a list of three integers for neon, argon, and krypton volumes. An input list with red 10 and blue 5 will output [135, 70, 0].

title: Blacksmith Forging Temperature Tracker
spec: The main function is `track(heat, strikes)`. Track the metal temperature by applying three distinct physical effects for each strike. First, identify the tool and force from the string. Second, apply the impact friction: a hammer adds triple the force to the heat, a mallet adds double, and a press adds the exact force. Third, apply the anvil cooling effect: subtract ten units of heat for a hammer, fifteen for a mallet, and thirty for a press. Fourth, enforce the ambient cooling limit: if the heat drops below room temperature which is twenty, it remains at twenty. Return the final heat integer. Starting with 500 and strikes hammer 10 and press 5 yields 510.

title: Glassblowing Annealing Schedule
spec: The target is `schedule(items)`. Determine the annealing times by calculating three distinct cooling phases for each item based on its thickness. First, compute the soaking phase: twenty minutes for every millimeter of thickness. Second, calculate the slow cooling phase: the square of the thickness multiplied by four. Third, determine the fast cooling phase: a flat duration of ninety minutes unless the thickness exceeds ten, in which case it requires one hundred and twenty minutes. Sum the three phases to find the total time for each item. Return a list of total times corresponding to each item. An input of [4, 12] returns the list [234, 936].

title: Roller Coaster Kinetic Energy Simulator
spec: Call `simulate(heights)`. Evaluate the coaster speed by analyzing three mechanical factors at each segment. First, determine the potential energy difference from the starting height, assuming a mass of one thousand and gravity of ten. Second, calculate the kinetic energy available, subtracting a friction loss of five hundred for every segment traversed so far. Third, convert the remaining kinetic energy into velocity using the square root of double the energy divided by mass. If the energy is zero or negative, the coaster stalls and velocity is zero. Return a list of velocities for each segment rounded down to the nearest integer. A track with heights 100, 90, and 80 produces [0, 13, 19].

title: Sailboat Rigging Tension Analyzer
spec: Start with `analyze(wind, sails)`. Assess the mechanical stress on the mast by breaking down the forces into three vectors. First, compute the total wind pressure by squaring the wind speed and multiplying by the sum of all integer sail areas. Second, distribute this load across the rigging: the forestay takes forty percent, the backstay takes thirty percent, and the shrouds take the remaining thirty percent. Third, apply a dynamic wave impact multiplier: if the wind speed exceeds fifteen, increase all loads by twenty five percent. Return a list of three integers for the forestay, backstay, and shrouds rounded down. For a wind of 10 and areas 10 and 20, the result is [1200, 900, 900].

title: Parachute Deployment Descent Calculator
spec: Function `calculate(altitudes)` evaluates the total descent time by summing three distinct flight phases. First, evaluate the freefall phase: altitude drops at sixty units per second until reaching the deployment height of one thousand. Second, compute the canopy inflation phase: taking exactly four seconds and consuming two hundred units of altitude. Third, calculate the gliding phase: the remaining altitude is covered at a safe descent rate of six units per second. If the initial altitude is too low for freefall, start inflation immediately. Return a list of descent times rounded down for each drop. With inputs 2000 and 1000, it returns [153, 137].

title: Typewriter Keystroke Jam Assessor
spec: Use `assess(text)`. Identify mechanical jams by evaluating the typewriter basket zones in three steps. First, filter the text to remove all spaces, numbers, and punctuation, converting everything to lowercase. Second, map each letter to its mechanical zone: letters a through h belong to the left zone, i through q to the middle zone, and r through z to the right zone. Third, scan the sequence for consecutive letters in the same zone; each occurrence constitutes one jam. Return the total integer count of jams. For the input string a b c 1 h q, the output is 3.

title: Printing Press Ink Consumption
spec: The function is `estimate(pages)`. Determine the ink requirements by separating the analysis into three distinct character groups. First, process alphabetical characters: each requires two units of cyan and one of black. Second, evaluate numerical digits: each requires three units of magenta and two of yellow. Third, analyze punctuation marks: each requires four units of black and one of yellow. Spaces require no ink. Sum the totals for all pages across the four colors. Return a list of four integers representing cyan, magenta, yellow, and black totals. Pages containing A1! and B2 require [4, 6, 3, 7].

title: Lighthouse Beam Visibility Predictor
spec: The entry point is `predict(conditions)`. Calculate the maximum visibility range by applying three atmospheric modifiers to the base beam. First, start with a base visibility of fifty miles. Second, apply the weather penalty: clear subtracts nothing, cloudy subtracts ten, rain subtracts twenty, and fog subtracts forty. Third, adjust for the moon phase extracted from the condition string containing words like full, half, or new: full adds five miles due to ambient light, half adds two, and new adds zero. Return a list of visibility ranges as integers. With inputs clear full and fog new, it gives [55, 10].

title: Geothermal Heat Pump Efficiency
spec: Use `evaluate(temperatures)`. Determine the system efficiency by processing the thermal exchange through three distinct stages. First, calculate the temperature differential between the ground and a fixed indoor target of seventy. Second, determine the heat transfer rate: multiply the differential by five for heating when the ground is colder, or by eight for cooling when the ground is warmer. Third, apply a compressor penalty: if the differential exceeds thirty, subtract twenty from the transfer rate to account for mechanical strain. Return a list of final transfer rates as integers. Inputs of 50 and 110 result in [100, 300].

title: Hydroelectric Dam Spillway Controller
spec: Start with `control(levels)`. Determine the number of open spillway gates by evaluating three safety criteria. First, compute the excess volume: any level above the critical threshold of one hundred generates ten units of excess water per level increment. Second, calculate the baseline gate requirement: one gate must be opened for every fifty units of excess water, rounded down. Third, apply the emergency surge protocol: if the level is rising and the current level exceeds one hundred and twenty, add two extra gates automatically. Return a list of integers representing the number of open gates for each level. For water levels 90, 110, and 130, the output is [0, 2, 8].

title: Volcano Ash Fall Forecaster
spec: The function `forecast(eruptions)` predicts the ash spread distance by calculating three dispersion factors. First, parse the string to extract the intensity level and wind speed integers. Second, calculate the base column height by multiplying the intensity by one thousand. Third, compute the horizontal spread: multiply the column height by the wind speed, then divide by a gravity constant of fifty. Fourth, apply a particle density modifier: if the intensity is greater than five, reduce the final spread by ten percent due to heavier ash. Return a list of spread distances rounded down to the nearest integer. With inputs 4 20 and 6 10, it returns [1600, 1080].

title: Cable Car Tension Monitor
spec: The function is `monitor(passengers)`. Calculate the cable tension by aggregating three load components for each car in the sequence. First, determine the static load of each car, fixed at two thousand units. Second, calculate the variable load: multiply the passenger count by one hundred and fifty units. Third, compute the dynamic stress factor: if adjacent cars have a passenger difference greater than ten, add a stress penalty of five hundred units to both cars. Sum the static, variable, and stress loads for each car. Return a list of total tension values for each car. For 5 and 20 passengers, it yields [3250, 5500].

title: Ferris Wheel Weight Distribution
spec: Use `balance(gondolas)`. The input is a list of strings representing passenger counts, formatted as adult and child integers separated by a space. Assess the structural balance by checking three symmetrical conditions. First, parse each string to extract adult and child counts. Second, calculate the total weight for each gondola: adults weigh eighty and children weigh forty. Third, find the diametrically opposite gondola, assuming an even number of total gondolas. Fourth, compute the weight difference between each pair of opposite gondolas. If the difference exceeds four hundred, flag that pair as unbalanced. Return the integer count of unbalanced pairs. With inputs 10 0 and 1 0 and 0 0 and 1 0, it returns 1.

title: Hovercraft Skirt Pressure Balancer
spec: The entry function `balance(pressures)` determines the necessary airflow adjustments by executing three diagnostic steps. First, calculate the average pressure across all four chambers. Second, identify the deviation of each chamber from this average. Third, formulate the required adjustment: if a chamber is below the average, it requires an inflation command equal to the difference; if above, it requires a deflation command equal to half the difference. Return a list of integers representing the adjustment values in the original order. Receiving 100, 120, 90, 130 returns [10, -5, 20, -10].

title: Drawbridge Winch Stress Analyzer
spec: Call `analyze(angles)`. Calculate the mechanical stress on the lifting winch through three geometric evaluations for each elevation angle. First, compute the effective weight load: the base weight of one hundred multiplied by the cosine-like factor, approximated as ninety minus the angle. Second, determine the wind resistance load: a flat five hundred units if the angle is between thirty and sixty inclusive. Third, apply a mechanical disadvantage multiplier: add twenty percent to the total accumulated load when the angle is less than twenty due to poor leverage. Return a list of total stress loads rounded down. Angles 10 and 45 produce [9600, 5000].

title: Carousel Horse Rotation Synchronizer
spec: Use `synchronize(horses)`. Determine the required vertical travel speed by evaluating three mechanical constraints. First, parse the string to extract the row as inner or outer and the size as small or large. Second, assign a base travel distance: outer row horses move forty units, inner row horses move thirty units. Third, adjust for size mass: large horses decrease the speed of movement, adding two seconds to the base cycle time of ten seconds, while small horses leave it unchanged. Calculate the speed as distance divided by cycle time. Return a list of speeds rounded down to the nearest integer. Descriptors outer large and inner small result in [3, 3].

title: Zip Line Velocity Predictor
spec: The function `predict(riders)` estimates the arrival velocity by computing three kinetic phases for each rider. First, calculate the initial acceleration force: the rider weight multiplied by a slope factor of three. Second, compute the aerodynamic drag: the square of the weight divided by fifty. Third, determine the net velocity at the end of the one hundred unit line: subtract the drag from the acceleration force, and multiply the result by two. If the net velocity falls below zero, it becomes zero. Return a list of arrival velocities as integers. With weights 60 and 100, it returns [216, 200].

title: Tramway Cable Wear Assessor
spec: Call `assess(trips)`. Calculate the degradation units for the cable by assessing three wear factors per trip. First, extract the weather condition and passenger count from the string. Second, compute the base friction wear: multiply the passenger count by four. Third, apply the environmental abrasive factor: snow adds fifty wear units, rain adds twenty, and clear adds zero. Fourth, check for extreme tension: if the passenger count exceeds forty, multiply the total trip wear by two. Accumulate the total wear units. Return the final integer wear sum. Trips snow 30 and clear 50 yield 570.

title: Snowplow Route Optimizer
spec: Start with `optimize(streets)`. Evaluate the priority score of each string street description containing length and snow depth separated by a space. First, parse the length and depth integers. Second, calculate the volume of snow: length multiplied by depth. Third, compute the disruption penalty: streets with a depth greater than twelve get an additional five hundred priority points. Fourth, determine the final score by adding the snow volume to the disruption penalty. Return a list of integer priority scores. Inputs 10 15 and 20 5 return [650, 100].

title: Garbage Truck Capacity Tracker
spec: Use `track(bins)`. Monitor the truck storage by simulating the compaction process in three steps. First, evaluate the initial intake: each bin adds its raw volume to the hopper. Second, apply the hydraulic compaction cycle: for every fifty units of raw trash, the compactor reduces the volume by forty percent, leaving sixty percent. Third, enforce the maximum truck capacity of one thousand units: if adding a compacted bin exceeds this, the bin is rejected and not added. Return a list of accepted compacted volumes rounded down to the nearest integer. With bin volumes 100, 60, and 2000, it gives [60, 36].

title: Escalator Step Maintenance Scheduler
spec: The function `schedule(usage)` determines the maintenance intervals by calculating three wear accumulation phases based on daily passenger counts. First, establish the baseline mechanical wear: each day accrues fifty units regardless of usage. Second, calculate the passenger load wear: every hundred passengers add ten units of wear. Third, identify heavy usage spikes: any day with over five thousand passengers adds a stress penalty of two hundred units. When the cumulative wear exceeds ten thousand, a maintenance cycle is triggered and wear resets to zero for the next day. Return the integer count of triggered maintenance cycles. For a twelve day list of 6000 each day, it yields 1.

title: Crane Lift Stability Evaluator
spec: Call `evaluate(loads)`. Assess the tipping risk by calculating three stability moments for each string load description. First, parse the weight and angle integers. Second, calculate the boom extension radius: subtract the angle from ninety and multiply by two. Third, compute the overturning moment: multiply the weight by the extension radius. Fourth, apply the counterweight offset: subtract a fixed stability threshold of five thousand from the moment. If the result is greater than zero, the lift is unstable. Return the integer count of unstable lifts. Given 20 60 and 200 30, it returns 1.

title: Subway Dwell Time Evaluator
spec: Write a program starting with `evaluate(trips)` to assess train delays. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains four integers representing arrival hour, arrival minute, departure hour, and departure minute. First, convert all times to total minutes since midnight. Second, calculate the dwell duration in minutes for each trip. Third, assess a severity penalty score if the duration exceeds five minutes. Finally, sum up all total penalties for the entire input. Example: [[14, 30, 14, 32], [15, 0, 15, 10]] returns 5 because the second trip dwells for ten minutes.

title: Alloy Density Calculator
spec: Create a module starting with `calculate(alloys)` to find specific metal properties. The input is a list of tuples where each tuple has a base mass, an additive mass, and a temperature expansion factor. First, compute the total raw mass by adding the two mass values. Second, determine the base volume by dividing the raw mass by a standard divisor of eight. Third, adjust this volume using the provided temperature expansion factor. Finally, return a list of final densities calculated as total mass divided by the adjusted volume. Example: [(80, 20, 1)] returns [12.5].

title: Tsunami Arrival Predictor
spec: Develop a tool starting with `predict(events)` to estimate wave travel times. The input is a list of tuples containing the origin distance in kilometers and the average ocean depth in meters. First, compute the gravity acceleration multiplier based on the ocean depth. Second, determine the raw wave speed by taking the square root of that acceleration. Third, calculate the travel time by dividing the distance by the speed and converting it to hours. Return a list of travel times rounded to the nearest whole hour. Example: [(1000, 4000)] returns [1].

title: Choral Arrangement Validator
spec: Write a script entry `score(arrangements)` to verify four-part harmonies. The input is a list of chords, where each chord is a tuple of four integer musical notes from zero to one hundred. First, verify that all notes fall within standard human vocal ranges. Second, check the progression for invalid parallel fifths between consecutive chords. Third, measure the chord spacing to ensure no adjacent voices are separated by more than an octave. Compile and return a list of boolean values representing whether each chord progression is valid. Example: [(40, 52, 64, 76), (41, 53, 65, 77)] returns [False].

title: Bridge Load Simulator
spec: Implement a structural check starting with `simulate(bridges)` to verify safety margins. The input is a list of parameter tuples containing span length, number of support cables, and average expected vehicle mass. First, calculate the static weight of the span itself. Second, distribute this static weight evenly across the available support cables. Third, add the dynamic stress from the vehicle mass to find the maximum peak load. Return a list of structural safety margins calculated as a ratio of peak load to maximum capacity. Example: [(100, 10, 2000)] returns [0.85].

title: Helicopter Rotor Lift Calculator
spec: Create an aerodynamic evaluator using `calculate(rotors)` for blade efficiency. The input is a list of tuples containing blade length, blade width, and rotation speed in revolutions per minute. First, calculate the total rotor disk swept area using the blade length. Second, determine the blade tip speed utilizing the length and rotation speed. Third, estimate the air density lifting factor based on standard atmospheric constants. Return a list of total upward lift forces measured in newtons. Example: [(5, 0.5, 300)] returns [45000.0].

title: Kite Aerodynamic Profiler
spec: Write a physics tool starting with `profile(kites)` to score flight stability. The input is a list of tuples containing kite width, height, bridle towing angle, and tail length. First, calculate the main sail surface area from the width and height. Second, determine the wind resistance factor caused by the towing angle. Third, evaluate the drag stabilization provided by the tail length. Return a list of integer stability scores ranging from one to ten. Example: [(100, 50, 45, 200)] returns [8].

title: Juggling Pattern Animator
spec: Develop a sequence validator using `validate(patterns)` to check siteswap notation. The input is a list of integer sequences representing the heights of juggling throws. First, calculate the average of the sequence to find the required number of objects. Second, check if this average is a whole number to ensure basic mathematical validity. Third, simulate landing times to check for orbit collisions where two objects land simultaneously. Return a list of boolean values indicating whether each pattern can actually be juggled. Example: [[4, 4, 1], [3, 2]] returns [True, False].

title: Vaccine Cold Chain Tracker
spec: Implement a compliance checker starting with `audit(shipments)` to ensure medication viability. The input is a list of lists containing integer temperature readings in Celsius. First, count any consecutive readings that rise above eight degrees. Second, scan for any single reading that drops below freezing. Third, calculate the cumulative heat exposure over the entire transit period. Return a list of string statuses evaluating each shipment as either safe or compromised. Example: [[2, 5, 4], [2, 10, 12, 10]] returns [safe, compromised].

title: Honeycomb Structure Analyzer
spec: Write a biological geometry tool using `analyze(combs)` to evaluate hive efficiency. The input is a list of tuples with cell radius, cell depth, and wall thickness. First, compute the hexagonal surface area based on the cell radius. Second, calculate the total wax volume required using the depth and thickness. Third, evaluate the structural efficiency by taking the ratio of internal volume to wax volume. Return a list of these efficiency ratios rounded to two decimal places. Example: [(5, 10, 1)] returns [2.15].

title: Firework Trajectory Plotter
spec: Create a safety script starting with `plot(fireworks)` for pyrotechnic displays. The input is a list of tuples containing shell mass, lift charge mass, and fuse duration in seconds. First, calculate the initial launch velocity generated by the lift charge. Second, determine the apex height using that velocity and standard gravity deceleration. Third, calculate the explosive burst radius based on the shell mass. Return a list of recommended minimum safe viewing distances in meters. Example: [(50, 10, 3)] returns [150.0].

title: Skateboard Trick Scorer
spec: Develop an extreme sports judge using `score(runs)` to total up event points. The input is a list of lists containing trick tuples of rotation degrees, flip count, and grind seconds. First, award base points for rotation by dividing the total degrees by ninety. Second, apply a multiplier to those points based on the flip count. Third, add a flat bonus score for any grind duration lasting longer than two seconds. Sum up the points for the entire run and return a list of total integer scores. Example: [[(360, 2, 1), (180, 1, 3)]] returns [13].

title: Watch Escapement Calibrator
spec: Write a mechanical horology script starting with `calibrate(movements)` to find time drift. The input is a list of tuples providing pendulum length, bob mass, and spring tension. First, calculate the theoretical base swing frequency using only the pendulum length. Second, apply a friction adjustment for air resistance using the bob mass. Third, factor in the extra kinetic energy added by the spring tension. Return a list of expected daily drift rates in seconds. Example: [(10, 50, 5)] returns [1.2].

title: Cave Exploration Mapper
spec: Implement a spelunking risk assessor using `map(expeditions)` to rate route safety. The input is a list of lists containing segment tuples of length, downward slope, and oxygen percentage. First, calculate the total underground depth reached by the end of the route. Second, identify the absolute minimum oxygen level encountered in any segment. Third, estimate the required physical exertion based on the total length and steepest slope. Return a list of string difficulty ratings categorizing each route as easy, moderate, or extreme. Example: [[(100, 10, 21), (50, 45, 19)]] returns [moderate].

title: Cheesemaking Coagulation Tracker
spec: Develop a dairy processing script starting with `track(batches)` to predict setting times. The input is a list of tuples containing milk volume in liters, starting temperature, and rennet drops. First, determine the temperature variance from the optimal thirty degrees. Second, calculate the specific rennet concentration per liter of milk. Third, estimate the enzyme activity speed combining the temperature variance and concentration. Return a list of expected coagulation times in minutes. Example: [(10, 32, 20)] returns [45].

title: Semaphore Flag Decoder
spec: Write a visual communication translator using `decode(signals)` to read messages. The input is a list of lists containing angle pairs representing left and right flag positions. First, normalize all incoming angles to standard forty five degree increments. Second, match each angle pair to its corresponding alphabet letter index. Third, identify resting positions and convert them to spaces between words. Return a list of fully decoded string messages. Example: [[(0, 45), (45, 90)]] returns [a b].

title: Water Slide Dynamics
spec: Create an amusement physics simulator starting with `simulate(slides)` to verify ride safety. The input is a list of tuples with vertical drop in meters, horizontal length, and water flow rate. First, calculate the average slope gradient of the flume. Second, determine the maximum terminal velocity factoring in the friction reduced by the water flow. Third, assess the splash impact force when the rider hits the bottom pool. Return a list of boolean values indicating whether each slide meets regulatory safety limits. Example: [(20, 50, 100)] returns [True].

title: Crochet Yarn Estimator
spec: Implement a crafting calculator using `estimate(patterns)` to find material requirements. The input is a list of lists containing tuples of a stitch type integer and a stitch count. First, assign a specific yarn length usage per stitch based on the type integer. Second, multiply that usage by the stitch count to get the length for that section. Third, add a standard ten percent error margin for tension variations. Sum the total for each pattern and return a list of required yardages. Example: [[(1, 100), (2, 50)]] returns [165.0].

title: Stadium Crowd Evacuation Modeler
spec: Develop a safety management tool starting with `model(sections)` to test clearance times. The input is a list of tuples containing person count, number of exit doors, and average walking speed. First, calculate the maximum flow rate per minute for the available exit doors. Second, determine the base walking time required to reach the exits. Third, add severe bottleneck delays for whenever the person count exceeds the flow rate. Return a list of expected total clearance times in minutes. Example: [(500, 2, 1)] returns [15.0].

title: Pasta Extrusion Pressure Monitor
spec: Write a culinary manufacturing script using `monitor(batches)` to check machinery stress. The input is a list of tuples containing flour mass, water mass, and extrusion speed. First, calculate the basic hydration ratio of the dough mixture. Second, determine the dough viscosity index which increases heavily as hydration drops. Third, multiply this viscosity by the extrusion speed to find the mechanical stress on the die. Return a list of expected pressure readings in bars. Example: [(1000, 300, 5)] returns [120.5].

title: Orchid Light Exposure Tracker
spec: Create a botanical care calculator starting with `track(plants)` to sum solar energy. The input is a list of lists containing daily tuples of morning sun hours, afternoon sun hours, and artificial light hours. First, multiply the morning hours by a gentle intensity factor. Second, multiply the afternoon hours by a harsh intensity factor. Third, add the artificial light multiplied by a constant low intensity factor. Sum up the week and return a list of total light accumulation values. Example: [[(3, 1, 4), (2, 0, 5)]] returns [45.0].

title: Fresco Plaster Drying Estimator
spec: Implement an art restoration tool using `estimate(walls)` to plan painting schedules. The input is a list of tuples containing plaster thickness in millimeters, room humidity percentage, and air temperature. First, calculate the base drying hours required solely from the plaster thickness. Second, multiply those hours by a moisture retention factor derived from the humidity. Third, decrease the required time based on how warm the ambient air temperature is. Return a list of expected curing times in hours. Example: [(10, 60, 22)] returns [48.0].

title: Rowing Regatta Pace Calculator
spec: Write a sports timing script starting with `calculate(crews)` for sprint predictions. The input is a list of tuples with stroke rate, distance per stroke, and headwind speed. First, calculate the base boat speed in meters per second. Second, subtract the kinetic resistance caused by the headwind speed. Third, determine the total time required to cover a standard two thousand meter course at that adjusted speed. Return a list of expected finish times in seconds. Example: [(30, 8, 2)] returns [400.0].

title: Violin Acoustic Resonance Evaluator
spec: Develop a luthier analysis tool using `evaluate(instruments)` to find tonal peaks. The input is a list of tuples containing wood density, carved plate thickness, and central arch height. First, compute the stiffness modulus from the raw density and thickness. Second, calculate the interior air volume affected by the arch height. Third, determine the primary resonant frequency by blending the stiffness and volume factors. Return a list of integer frequencies representing the dominant tone in hertz. Example: [(400, 3, 15)] returns [280].

title: Neonatal Incubator Climate Tracker
spec: Write a biomedical monitoring script starting with `track(incubators)` to manage thermal stability. The input is a list of tuples containing ambient room temperature, baby mass in kilograms, and desired core temperature. First, calculate the rapid heat loss rate to the colder room. Second, determine the metabolic heat naturally generated by the baby mass. Third, compute the thermal deficit required to maintain the desired core temperature perfectly. Return a list of target heater outputs in watts. Example: [(20, 2, 37)] returns [150.0].

title: Planetary Alignment Calculator
spec: Write a small module to determine if a set of planets are aligned within a specific tolerance. Define a function `alignments(planets)` that takes a list of tuples containing the planet name, its orbital radius, and its current angle in degrees. The module must contain separate helper functions to calculate the angular difference between any two planets, to check if a list of angles falls within a single ten degree sector, and to predict the next number of days until a rough alignment occurs assuming circular orbits and given orbital periods. The entry function returns a list of planet names that are currently aligned. Example: giving earth at twenty degrees and mars at twenty five degrees returns their names.

title: Photosynthesis Rate Estimator
spec: Calculate the estimated rate of photosynthesis for a plant given environmental factors. The entry function `photosynthesis(conditions)` accepts a list of numeric tuples representing light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature. Create separate helper functions to calculate the light limitation factor, the carbon dioxide limitation factor, and the temperature curve using a bell-shaped response. Another helper should combine these using Liebig law of the minimum to find the overall limiting factor and return a final rate between zero and one hundred. Example: given an intensity of five hundred, carbon dioxide of four hundred, and temperature of twenty five, it might return a rate of eighty.

title: Shipping Container Packer
spec: Estimate how many identical rectangular boxes can fit inside a standard shipping container. The function `pack(dimensions)` receives a tuple of length, width, and height of a single box. Write distinct helper functions to evaluate the number of boxes that fit in a specific orientation, to rotate the box dimensions through all six possible three dimensional alignments, and to calculate the unused volume for a given packed configuration. The main function should iterate through all orientations, use the helpers to find the one that yields the maximum number of boxes, and return this maximum count. Example: a box of size two by two by two fitting in a container of size ten by ten by ten returns one hundred and twenty five.

title: Gear Train Ratio Calculator
spec: Determine the overall mechanical advantage and speed ratio of a compound gear train. The entry function `gears(train)` accepts a list of pairs representing the number of teeth on the driving gear and the driven gear for each stage. Implement separate helper functions to compute the ratio of a single gear pair, to multiply a sequence of ratios for the entire train, and to calculate the final output speed given an input speed of one thousand revolutions per minute. The main function returns a tuple containing the overall mechanical advantage and the output speed. Example: a train with pairs twenty and forty, then ten and thirty, returns an advantage of six and a speed of one hundred sixty six.

title: Inflation Adjustment Calculator
spec: Calculate the present value of historical prices using annual inflation rates. The function `inflate(records)` takes a list of tuples containing a year, a price, and a target year, along with a separate list of historical inflation rates for each year. Write independent helper functions to extract the sequence of rates between two given years, to compound the inflation multiplier over a period, and to apply this multiplier to a specific currency value. The entry function applies these helpers to each record and returns a list of adjusted prices. Example: a price of ten in year zero with an annual rate of five percent for two years returns eleven point zero two.

title: Reaction Yield Calculator
spec: Compute the theoretical and percent yield of a chemical reaction given the masses of reactants. The entry function `yields(reactants)` receives a list of tuples containing reactant name, molar mass, stoichiometric coefficient, and actual mass used, plus the actual product mass obtained. You must implement helper functions to convert mass to moles for each reactant, to determine the limiting reactant by dividing moles by the stoichiometric coefficient, and to calculate the theoretical mass of the product. The main function returns the limiting reactant name and the percent yield as a tuple. Example: giving inputs that should theoretically produce fifty grams but actually produced forty grams returns the limiting reactant and eighty.

title: Projectile Motion Simulator
spec: Simulate the flight path of a projectile subject to gravity and air resistance. The function `trajectory(initials)` accepts a tuple of initial velocity, launch angle in degrees, and a drag coefficient. Provide separate helper functions to resolve the initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components, to calculate the acceleration at any given time due to drag and gravity, and to step through time integrating position and velocity using small intervals. The entry function returns the total horizontal distance traveled before the vertical position drops below zero. Example: an initial velocity of fifty at forty five degrees with zero drag returns roughly two hundred and fifty five.

title: Dead Reckoning Calculator
spec: Estimate a ship final position based on a starting coordinate, speed, heading, and time elapsed. The function `navigate(legs)` takes a starting coordinate tuple and a list of movement legs, each being a tuple of speed in knots, heading in degrees, and hours traveled. Write dedicated helper functions to convert degrees to radians, to calculate the horizontal and vertical distance for a single leg, and to update a geographic coordinate based on small displacements. The main function returns the final estimated latitude and longitude as a tuple. Example: starting at zero and zero, traveling at ten knots north for two hours, returns a final position translated twenty nautical miles north.

title: Room Reverberation Time Estimator
spec: Estimate the acoustic reverberation time of a rectangular room using the Sabine formula. The entry function `reverberation(room)` takes room dimensions length, width, and height, followed by a list of tuples detailing surface area and absorption coefficient for different materials present. Include helper functions to calculate the total room volume, to compute the total sound absorption area by summing the products of area and coefficient, and to apply the Sabine equation. The entry function returns the estimated time in seconds. Example: a small room with highly reflective walls might return a time of two point five seconds.

title: Lens System Focal Length Calculator
spec: Calculate the effective focal length of a system of thin lenses placed in a row. The function `lenses(system)` accepts a list of tuples where each tuple contains the focal length of a lens and the distance to the next lens. You should write separate helper functions to calculate the optical power of a single lens, to compute the combined power of two thin lenses separated by a distance using the Gullstrand equation, and to sequentially reduce a list of lenses into a single effective focal length. The function returns the final effective focal length. Example: two lenses of focal length ten separated by a distance of five return an effective focal length of six point six six.

title: Population Growth Simulator
spec: Model the growth of an animal population considering birth rates, death rates, and carrying capacity. The function `population(parameters)` takes an initial population, carrying capacity, intrinsic growth rate, and number of years to simulate. Develop individual helper functions to calculate the logistic growth increment for a single year, to adjust the increment based on a random environmental fluctuation factor, and to bound the population so it never drops below zero. The entry function returns a list of population counts for each year. Example: starting with ten animals and a capacity of one hundred, the sequence gradually approaches one hundred over the specified years.

title: Watershed Runoff Estimator
spec: Calculate the total volume of surface runoff from a watershed after a rainfall event. The entry function `runoff(areas)` accepts a rainfall depth in millimeters and a list of land segments, each given as a tuple of area in square meters and a runoff coefficient. Write distinct helper functions to calculate the runoff volume for a single segment, to sum volumes across multiple segments, and to convert the total volume into cubic dekameters for large scale reporting. The main function returns this final total volume. Example: a fifty millimeter rain on a two thousand square meter parking lot with a high coefficient returns a large volume compared to a forest.

title: Wind Chill and Heat Index Calculator
spec: Determine the perceived temperature based on actual temperature, wind speed, and humidity. The function `perceived(weather)` takes a list of tuples containing temperature in celsius, wind speed in kilometers per hour, and relative humidity percentage. Implement independent helper functions to calculate the wind chill for cold temperatures, to calculate the heat index for warm temperatures using the standard polynomial formula, and to determine which formula is appropriate for a given set of conditions. The entry function returns a list of perceived temperatures. Example: a temperature of minus five with a wind speed of twenty returns a perceived temperature significantly lower than minus five.

title: Meat Roasting Time Estimator
spec: Estimate the total cooking time and resting time for a roast based on its weight and desired doneness. The function `roast(details)` receives the meat type, weight in kilograms, and a target internal temperature. Create separate helper functions to determine the base cooking time per kilogram for the specific meat, to adjust the time based on the target internal temperature, and to calculate the required resting time which is a percentage of the active cooking time. The function returns a tuple of cooking time and resting time in minutes. Example: a two kilogram beef roast targeting medium rare might return ninety minutes of cooking and twenty minutes of resting.

title: Crop Yield Predictor
spec: Predict the final yield of a wheat crop based on seasonal rainfall, fertilizer applied, and average temperature. The function `harvest(season)` takes a tuple containing total rainfall in millimeters, nitrogen applied in kilograms per hectare, and average temperature in celsius. Include separate helper functions to calculate the rainfall benefit score, to evaluate the nitrogen yield multiplier using diminishing returns, and to apply a temperature penalty if the average exceeds twenty five degrees. The main function combines these factors to return the estimated yield in tons per hectare. Example: adequate rain and optimal nitrogen without heat stress returns a high yield like four point five.

title: Seismic Wave Travel Time Calculator
spec: Calculate the time it takes for primary and secondary seismic waves to reach a recording station. The function `seismic(event)` receives the depth of the earthquake, the distance to the station on the surface, and the average velocities of primary and secondary waves. Develop helper functions to calculate the straight line distance through the crust from the hypocenter to the station, to compute the travel time for a specific wave type, and to find the time difference between the arrival of the two waves. The entry function returns this time difference. Example: an earthquake deep underground with a station far away will result in a time difference of several seconds.

title: Predator Prey Dynamics Simulator
spec: Simulate the populations of foxes and rabbits over time using the Lotka Volterra equations. The function `dynamics(initials)` accepts a tuple of initial rabbit population, initial fox population, and a sequence of four interaction rates. Write separate helper functions to compute the rate of change for the rabbit population, to compute the rate of change for the fox population, and to perform a numerical integration step to update both populations for a small time increment. The entry function simulates one hundred time steps and returns the final populations as a tuple. Example: starting with high rabbits and low foxes, the rabbit population initially grows then drops as foxes increase.

title: Tree Canopy Coverage Estimator
spec: Estimate the total shadow area cast by a collection of trees at noon. The function `canopy(trees)` receives a list of trees, each represented by a tuple of x and y coordinates and the canopy radius. Implement distinct helper functions to calculate the circular area of a single tree canopy, to compute the center to center distance between two trees, and to estimate the overlap area between two intersecting canopies using basic geometry. The main function calculates the total area minus the overlaps of intersecting pairs and returns the estimated shadow area. Example: two trees with radius ten located far apart return an area of roughly six hundred and twenty eight.

title: Staircase Dimension Calculator
spec: Calculate the optimal number of steps, riser height, and tread depth for a new staircase. The entry function `stairs(height)` takes the total vertical height to climb in millimeters. Provide helper functions to determine the ideal number of steps by dividing the height by a standard riser height and rounding, to calculate the exact riser height for that number of steps, and to determine the appropriate tread depth using the classic architectural rule that twice the riser plus the tread should equal six hundred and thirty. The function returns a tuple of step count, riser height, and tread depth. Example: a height of two thousand six hundred millimeters returns fourteen steps, a riser of one hundred eighty five, and a tread of two hundred sixty.

title: Board Foot Calculator
spec: Calculate the total board footage and cost for a woodworking project. The function `lumber(pieces)` accepts a list of tuples containing the quantity, thickness in inches, width in inches, length in feet, and price per board foot for various wood pieces. Write separate helper functions to calculate the board feet for a single piece of lumber, to multiply by quantity to get the total volume for a batch, and to calculate the cost for a batch. The entry function computes the total board feet and total cost across all pieces and returns them as a tuple. Example: ten pieces of two by four lumber eight feet long at two dollars per board foot returns fifty three point three board feet and a cost of one hundred six.

title: Decathlon Score Calculator
spec: Calculate the total points earned in a decathlon based on athlete performances. The function `decathlon(results)` receives a list of performance values for ten track and field events in standard order. Develop helper functions to calculate points for track events where lower times are better, to calculate points for field events where higher distances are better, and to apply the specific mathematical formula using standard event parameters for a given event index. The main function aggregates the points from all ten events and returns the total score. Example: a strong performance across all events will return a score in the range of seven to eight thousand points.

title: Aircraft Center of Gravity Calculator
spec: Determine if an aircraft is balanced within safe limits before takeoff. The function `balance(loads)` takes a list of items on the aircraft, each represented by a tuple of weight and its station arm distance from the datum line. Implement individual helper functions to calculate the moment of a single item by multiplying weight by arm, to sum the total weight and total moments of all items, and to calculate the center of gravity by dividing total moment by total weight. The entry function returns the center of gravity and a boolean indicating if it falls between the safe limits of eighty five and ninety five. Example: a total weight of two thousand and a moment of one hundred eighty thousand returns an arm of ninety and a safe status.

title: Anchor Chain Length Calculator
spec: Calculate the recommended length of anchor chain to deploy based on water depth and weather conditions. The function `anchor(conditions)` accepts a water depth in meters, wind speed in knots, and the height of the bow roller above the water. Write separate helper functions to calculate the total vertical distance from the seabed to the bow, to determine the appropriate scope ratio based on the wind speed, and to calculate the final chain length required. The entry function returns the required chain length in meters. Example: a depth of ten meters, bow height of two meters, and light wind requiring a scope of five returns a chain length of sixty meters.
